# Benchmark receipts — provenance

These JSON files are the raw measurement receipts behind the numbers cited in
`docs/benchmark.md`. Most are carried over byte-verbatim from the research runs
that validated the decoders before this package was extracted; receipts marked
*(in-repo)* below were generated by scripts in `bench/` after extraction.

| File | What it is | Hardware / env |
|---|---|---|
| `zoo_grid.json` | Matched cross-decoder logical-error-rate (LER) grid on the [[72,12,6]] bivariate-bicycle code, 6 rounds, SI1000 noise, p ∈ {0.001, 0.002, 0.003, 0.005} × basis ∈ {X, Z}. One shared DEM per cell (sha256-pinned), one shot set (seed 0), every decoder decoding identical shots. Decoders: ldpc BP / BP-OSD-0 / BP-OSD-10 / BP-LSD, Tesseract (MLE anchor), Relay-BP (Rust), sliding-window. The per-cell `dem_hash` values here are the byte-fidelity gate for this package's test fixtures, and the per-decoder `fails` counts are the no-regression targets. | CPU. python 3.12.12, numpy 2.2.6, stim 1.15.0, ldpc 2.4.1, relay-bp 0.2.2, tesseract-decoder 0.1.1.dev20260526203925 |
| `prereg.json` | The pre-registration committed before the grid ran: decoder configs, tie-break policies, shots-per-cell sizing, binding statistics. Provenance companion to `zoo_grid.json`. | n/a (plan document) |
| `bench_triton_results.json` | Triton min-sum BP kernel vs the torch edge-list baseline: one-iteration hard agreement, full-decode LER identity (156 = 156 = 156 fails / 2000 shots for numpy / torch / Triton), and decode_batch throughput at batch 256–16384. | NVIDIA H200, CUDA 12.4, torch 2.4.1+cu124, triton 3.0.0 |
| `bench_relay_triton.json` | Triton Relay-BP vs the `relay_bp` Rust oracle (F64): pre-leg posterior max-diff 1.8e-15, memory-term per-bit agreement 99.96%, full-relay LER identity (oracle 31 vs Triton 38 fails / 2000 shots, overlapping Wilson CIs), fp32/fp64 throughput. | NVIDIA H200, CUDA 12.4, torch 2.4.1, triton 3.0.0 |
| `bench_relay_mi300x.json` | The same Relay-BP validation re-run unmodified on AMD: identical primitive-identity numbers (pre-leg max-diff 1.8e-15) and the same oracle-vs-Triton LER identity (31 vs 38 / 2000), plus MI300X throughput. The dual-vendor portability receipt. | AMD MI300X (gfx942), ROCm 7.0.0, torch 2.9.0.dev+rocm7.0.0, triton 3.4.0+rocm7.0.0 |
| `bench_cudaq_compare.json` | Comparison against NVIDIA CUDA-Q QEC 0.6.0's GPU Relay-BP on the same 2000-shot workload: LER and throughput for both. **Read with the config-asymmetry caveat in `docs/benchmark.md`** — the CUDA-Q decoder was run with its own configuration surface, not a parameter-matched replica of ours. | NVIDIA H200, CUDA-Q QEC 0.6.0, torch 2.4.1+cu124 |
| `surface_cpu.json` *(in-repo)* | Surface-code memory LER receipts (second code family): tridec min-sum BP (torch CPU fp64, raw DEM) vs PyMatching (decomposed DEM), rotated memory-Z, (d=3, r=3) and (d=5, r=5) at p ∈ {0.003, 0.005}, 50,000 shots/cell, seed 20260610. Generated by `bench/surface_cpu.py`. Honest reading in `docs/benchmark.md` §3.4: plain BP loses to matching on surface codes, by design of the comparison. | CPU (darwin/arm64, Apple M4 Max). python 3.12.12, stim 1.15.0, pymatching 2.3.1, torch 2.12.0, numpy 2.2.6 |
| `latency_results.json` | Per-decoder latency/throughput sweep (CPU decoders + torch BP + Triton BP) with bootstrap CIs on per-syndrome latency, batch 1–16384. | NVIDIA H200 + host CPU; torch 2.4.1+cu124, triton 3.0.0 |
| `surface_relay_metal_preliminary.json` *(in-repo)* | **PRELIMINARY / EXPERIMENTAL** — Relay-BP on surface-code memory via the experimental Metal backend (fp32), 2000 shots/cell, vs plain BP and PyMatching on the same shots. Directional only; kept as the Metal-path record — the official numbers are in `surface_relay_mi300x.json`. Generated by `bench/surface_relay_metal.py`. | Apple M4 Max (darwin/arm64), triton 3.7.0 + triton-metal, torch 2.9.1, python 3.14.4 |
| `metal_spike.md` *(in-repo)* | Spike receipt for the EXPERIMENTAL Apple-silicon path: both Triton kernels (BP + Relay-BP, fp32) pass the existing correctness gates via triton-metal with zero source changes; BP 37–56× the per-shot numpy baseline, Relay-BP correct but launch-bound (31 s / 2000 shots). Re-validated through the public `backend="metal"` API by `tests/test_metal.py`. | Apple M4 Max (darwin/arm64), triton 3.7.0 (source build), triton-metal, torch 2.9.1 |
| `mi300x_packaged.json` *(in-repo, v0.1.0)* | PACKAGED-library validation on AMD: full test suite (88 passed, 10 skipped — GPU tiers bound on gfx942, darwin-only strict tiers skip) + benches through the installed package's public API on the canonical BB .dem fixture: BP triton 166 = numpy 166 fails / 2000 platform-local shots; Relay-BP triton fp32 34 vs Rust oracle 31 (98.8% per-shot agreement, overlapping CIs); Relay throughput within ±2.2% of the carried `bench_relay_mi300x.json` (514 vs 526 µs/syndrome @2000, 281 vs 278 @8192). Note: a first suite run with UNPINNED stim 1.16.0 had 2 statistical-tier plain-BP count checks land 5.7% off the pins (bar 5%, CIs overlapped); under the documented pin stim==1.15.0 the suite is fully green — the receipt records the pinned run. Generated by `bench/mi300x_packaged.py`. | AMD MI300X VF (gfx942), ROCm 7.0, torch 2.9.0.dev+rocm7.0.0, triton 3.4.0+rocm7.0.0, stim 1.15.0, ldpc 2.4.1, relay-bp 0.2.2 |
| `surface_relay_mi300x.json` *(in-repo, v0.1.0)* | **OFFICIAL Relay-BP surface receipts** (the §3.4 TODO closed): rotated memory-Z, (d=3, r=3) and (d=5, r=5) at p ∈ {0.003, 0.005}, 50,000 shots/cell, seed 20260610, Relay-BP + plain BP (packaged API, triton fp32, raw DEM) vs PyMatching (decomposed DEM) on the SAME host-local shots. Honest reading: Relay-BP ≈ MWPM at d=3 (overlapping CIs), but trails MWPM 3.8–4.3× at d=5 (disjoint CIs). Generated by `bench/surface_relay_gpu.py`. | AMD MI300X VF (gfx942), ROCm 7.0, torch 2.9, triton 3.4, pymatching 2.4.0, stim 1.15.0 |
| `full_grid_noregression.json` *(in-repo, v0.1.0)* | Full-grid EXACT no-regression: all 8 BB cells × ldpc-family adapters (BP, BPOSD-0, BPOSD-10, BPLSD) through `run_matched` at zoo_grid's exact shots/seed. Result: **31/32 counts EXACT** (24/24 for the deterministic BP/BPOSD adapters); the single deviation is BPLSD p=0.002/X (879 vs 880, one shot in 200k), attributed by the in-receipt `bplsd_determinism_probe` (same env, identical shots, fresh instances: counts flip between 879 and 880) to run-to-run nondeterminism inside ldpc's BpLsdDecoder — not a tridec regression. Generated by `bench/full_grid_noregression.py` + `bench/probe_bplsd_determinism.py`. | Receipt env: Apple M4 Max (darwin/arm64), python 3.12.12, stim 1.15.0, ldpc 2.4.1 |
| `megakernel_metal_spike.json` / `.md` *(in-repo, megakernel branch)* | **PRELIMINARY** — issue #2 spike: single-launch persistent BP / Relay-BP megakernels on the experimental triton-metal environment (fp32, block=32 — triton-metal silently drops `tl.debug_barrier`; see the .md). All correctness gates green; relay decode_batch(2000) 30.0 s → 0.46 s (65×, launch-overhead recovery). Generated by `bench/megakernel_metal.py`. | Apple M4 Max (darwin/arm64), triton 3.7.0 + triton-metal, torch 2.9.1, python 3.14.4 |
| `megakernel_h200.json` / `.md` *(in-repo, megakernel branch)* | **v0.2 CUDA megakernel receipts**: barrier sanity (CUDA honors `tl.debug_barrier` — behavioral ring repro + PTX `bar.sync` counts), 14/14 gates at BLOCK=128 AND 256 including the fp64 relay gates Metal couldn't run, the 24-config BLOCK×num_warps autotune sweep (every config correctness-gated), and decode_batch throughput/latency vs the v0.1 two-kernel path at batch 1–16384, same pod/same data. Generated by `bench/megakernel_cuda.py`. | NVIDIA H200, CUDA 12.4, torch 2.4.1+cu124, triton 3.0.0, python 3.11.10 |

## Modifications

All files are byte-identical copies of the originals, except:

- `latency_results.json`: re-serialized via `json.dump(..., indent=1)`, and the
  single field `env.gpu_clock.lock_note` was reworded to remove the cloud
  provider's name ("clock-locking not permitted on the cloud GPU container (no
  permission); clocks left at default"). No measurement values were changed.
